name: Julie Kallini
title: PhD student at Stanford University, USA
bio: Julie is a fourth-year Computer Science PhD student at Stanford, advised by Chris Potts and Dan Jurafsky. Her research spans computational linguistics, tokenization, efficient language model architectures, and byte-level modeling.

episodes.title: Can AI Learn Languages Humans Can't? Impossible Languages &  Tokenization, with Julie Kallini

name: Dr. Greta Tuckute
title: Research Fellow at the Kempner Institute, Harvard University, USA
bio: Dr. Greta Tuckute is a Kempner Research Fellow at the Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence at Harvard University, where she works at the intersection of neuroscience, cognitive science and AI. Her research follows three directions: precisely characterizing the neural architecture that supports language processing in the human brain, testing whether brains and artificial neural networks share representations and computational principles during language processing, and building biologically inspired models that learn language in more human-like ways. Originally from Lithuania, she earned her BSc and MSc at the University of Copenhagen and her PhD in Brain and Cognitive Sciences at MIT. She was named one of MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35.

episodes.title: What Makes a Sentence Memorable? Inside Language, Memory and LLMs, with Dr. Greta Tuckute

name: Dr. Elisa Kreiss
title: Assistant Professor of Communication at UCLA, USA
bio: Dr. Elisa Kreiss is an Assistant Professor of Communication at UCLA, where she leads the CoALAS Lab. Her work combines natural language processing, psycholinguistics and human-computer interaction to understand how communicative context shapes language use, with a particular focus on how we produce and understand language situated in the visual world. Her research has direct applications to image accessibility, the challenge of automatically generating image descriptions for blind and low-vision users, and includes datasets and metrics such as Concadia and ContextRef. She received her PhD in Linguistics from Stanford University in 2023 and a BS in Cognitive Science from Osnabrück University. Her work has been supported by a Google Research Award and Stanford HAI, and she received Stanford's Community Impact Award in 2022.

episodes.title: Is an Image Worth a Thousand Words? Hidden Failures of Multimodal Metrics, with Dr. Elisa Kreiss

name: Dr. Malihe Alikhani
title: Assistant Professor at Northeastern University, USA
bio: Dr. Malihe Alikhani is an Assistant Professor in the Khoury College of Computer Sciences at Northeastern University, where her research goal is to design inclusive and equitable language technologies that communicate effectively with diverse populations. Her work spans natural language processing, machine learning and AI ethics, with a focus on safe and fair AI systems that support communication and decision-making. Before joining Northeastern, she spent three years as an Assistant Professor at the University of Pittsburgh. She earned her PhD in Computer Science from Rutgers University. She served as an AAAS Science and Technology Congressional AI Fellow, is a visiting fellow at the Brookings Center on Regulation and Markets, and serves as Ethics Chair of ACL Rolling Review.

episodes.title: Is Your AI Just Flattering You? Sycophancy, AI Policies, and More, with Dr. Malihe Alikhani

name: Dr. Anna Ivanova
title: Assistant Professor at Georgia Tech, USA
bio: Dr. Anna (Anya) Ivanova is an Assistant Professor of Psychology at the Georgia Institute of Technology, where she leads the Language, Intelligence & Thought (LIT) Lab. Her research examines the relationship between language and thought in humans and in large language models, combining human brain imaging, behavioral studies and computational modeling. She co-led the influential paper "Dissociating Language and Thought in Large Language Models", which distinguishes formal linguistic competence from functional reasoning abilities, and developed the EWoK framework for evaluating world knowledge in language models. She received her PhD from MIT's Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences and completed her postdoctoral training at the MIT Quest for Intelligence. In 2024, she was named to MIT Technology Review's 35 Innovators Under 35.

episodes.title: Can Language Alone Create Intelligence? Insights from Neuroscience and AI, with Dr. Anna Ivanova

name: Dr. Saadia Gabriel
title: Assistant Professor at UCLA, USA
bio: Dr. Saadia Gabriel is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering, where she leads the Misinformation, AI and Responsible Society (MARS) Lab, and an affiliated faculty member of the Bunche Center for African-American Studies. Her research focuses on measuring the factuality and intent of human-written language and on the gap between scalability and safety in LLMs. She earned her PhD at the University of Washington, co-advised by Yejin Choi and Franziska Roesner, then was an MIT CSAIL postdoctoral fellow and an NYU Data Science Faculty Fellow. With Microsoft researchers, she developed (De)ToxiGen for detecting hate speech and toxic language. She was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 and received an Amazon Research Award for AI for African languages.

episodes.title: From Hate Speech to Best Paper: Building Safer AI Systems, with Dr. Saadia Gabriel (Part 1)
100% Jailbreak Success? The Hard Truth About AI Safety, with Dr. Saadia Gabriel (Part 2)

name: Dr. Hila Gonen
title: Assistant Professor at the University of British Columbia, Canada
bio: Dr. Hila Gonen is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the University of British Columbia and a Canada CIFAR AI Chair at Amii. Her research lies at the intersection of natural language processing and machine learning, with a long-term vision of making LLMs responsible, reliable and trustworthy systems that are fair across languages and socio-demographic groups. She works on understanding and controlling model behavior, on reliability, safety and bias mitigation, and on multilingual NLP, and has recently become interested in applying NLP to health. Before joining UBC, she was a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Washington, Meta AI and Amazon. She earned her PhD in Computer Science at Bar-Ilan University and her MSc at the Hebrew University. Her work received best paper awards at CoNLL 2019 and RepL4NLP 2022.

episodes.title: Does Liking Yellow Make You a School Bus Driver? Hidden Failures in LLMs, with Dr. Hila Gonen

name: Dr. Letitia Parcalabescu
title: Creator of the AI Coffee Break YouTube channel
bio: Dr. Letitia Parcalabescu is an AI researcher at Aleph Alpha Research in Heidelberg, where she works on training reasoning models that are interpretable by design and on curating and synthesizing data for large-scale pre-training. With an academic background in physics and computer science, she earned her PhD in Computational Linguistics at Heidelberg University in 2024, supervised by Anette Frank. Her thesis, "Measuring the Contributions of Vision and Text Modalities in Multimodal Transformers", introduced new metrics for studying how vision-language models combine images and text, and how self-consistent and faithful their explanations are. Since 2020, she has run the YouTube channel "AI Coffee Break with Letitia", where the animated Ms. Coffee Bean explains the latest AI research in short, accessible videos. She is also a KlarText award winner for science communication.

episodes.title: Faithfulness and Hallucinations in Reasoning Models, with Dr. Letitia Parcalabescu

name: Dr. Swabha Swayamdipta
title: Assistant Professor at the University of Southern California, USA
bio: Dr. Swabha Swayamdipta is a Gabilan Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the USC Viterbi School of Engineering, where she has led the Data, Interpretability, Language and Learning (DILL) Lab since 2022. Her research in natural language processing and machine learning examines how datasets are constructed and how they shape model decisions, as well as the interpretability and evaluation of language models. She is also Associate Director of the USC Center for AI and Society and an Amazon Scholar. She received her PhD from the Language Technologies Institute at Carnegie Mellon University, advised by Noah Smith and Chris Dyer, followed by a postdoc at the Allen Institute for AI. Her recognitions include an Intel Rising Star Faculty Award and the AI2 Young Investigators Award.

episodes.title: AI Safety Beyond Benchmarks --  Dr. Swabha Swayamdipta on Evaluation, Personalization, and Control

name: Dr. Maria Ryskina
title: CIFAR AI Safety Postdoctoral Fellow at the Vector Institute for AI, Canada
bio: Dr. Maria Ryskina is a CIFAR AI Safety Postdoctoral Fellow at the Vector Institute for AI, where she works with Prof. Gillian Hadfield on interdisciplinary approaches to AI alignment, focusing on how multi-agent interaction can help normative reasoning emerge in large language models. Her research spans AI, natural language processing, linguistics and the cognitive and behavioural sciences. Previously, she was a postdoc in Ev Fedorenko's lab at MIT, using methods from cognitive neuroscience and NeuroAI to study how concepts are represented in the brain and in large language models. She completed her PhD at Carnegie Mellon University's Language Technologies Institute, modelling non-standard language use and the evolution of language norms, and earned her BSc and MSc at MIPT and Skoltech. She is a core organizer of Queer in AI.

episodes.title: Do LLMs Understand Meaning? Neuroscience, Evaluation, and the Future of AI, with Dr. Maria Ryskina

name: Dr. Maria Antoniak
title: Assistant Professor at the University of Colorado Boulder, USA
bio: Dr. Maria Antoniak is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the University of Colorado Boulder, also affiliated with Information Science, where she leads the Antoniak Lab. Her research lies at the intersection of natural language processing and cultural analytics, with applications to narrative medicine, computational humanities and online communities. Her recent work studies personal disclosures in human-LLM conversations, storytelling across online communities, NLP for maternal healthcare, and writing across research cultures. Before joining CU Boulder, she was a Young Investigator at the Allen Institute for AI and a postdoc at the Pioneer Centre for AI at the University of Copenhagen. She earned her PhD in Information Science at Cornell University, advised by David Mimno, and her master's in Computational Linguistics at the University of Washington.

episodes.title: How Does AI Reflect Society, with Dr. Maria Antoniak

name: Dr. Annie En-Shiun Lee
title: Assistant professor at the OntarioTech University and the University of Toronto (status-only), Canada
bio: Annie En-Shiun Lee is an assistant professor at the OntarioTech University and the University of Toronto (status-only). Her goal is to make language technology as inclusive and accessible to as many people as possible. She runs the Lee Language Lab (L^3) with research focusing on language diversity and multilinguality. Professor Lee’s research has been published in Nature Digital Medicine, ACM Computing Surveys, ACL, SIGCSE, IEEE TKDE, and Bioinformatics. She serves as the demo co-chair for NAACL and has extensive experience transferring technology to industry.

episodes.title: Multilingual AI, with Dr. Annie En-Shiun Lee

name: Dr. Vered Shwartz
title: Assistant professor at the University of British Columbia, Canada
bio: Vered Shwartz is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at the University of British Columbia, and a CIFAR AI Chair at the Vector Institute. Her research interests focus on natural language processing, with the fundamental goal of building models capable of human-level understanding of natural language. Her lab is currently working on testing and improving the capabilities of large language models and vision and language models, developing culturally-competent AI, and responsible NLP applications in sensitive domains (e.g., legal, medical).

episodes.title: Why AI Doesn’t Understand Your Culture? Dr. Vered Shwartz on Cultural Bias in LLMs

name: Dr. Ana Marasović
title: Assistant professor at the University of Utah, USA
bio: Ana Marasović is an Assistant Professor in the Kahlert School of Computing at the University of Utah. Her research interests broadly fall into natural language processing (NLP), human-centered AI, and interpretability. Previously, she was a Young Investigator at the Allen Institute for AI, and during that time, also held a courtesy appointment in the Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering at the University of Washington. She received her PhD from Heidelberg University. She is a co-recipient of the Best Paper Award at ACL 2023, the Best Paper Honorable Mention at ACL 2020, and the Best Paper Award at the SoCal 2022 NLP Symposium. She is also the University of Utah One-U Responsible AI Initiative Faculty Fellow.

episodes.title: Can We Trust AI Explanations? Dr. Ana Marasović on AI Trustworthiness, Explainability & Faithfulness

name: Dr. Valentina Pyatkin
title: Postdoc at the Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington, USA
bio: Valentina Pyatkin is a postdoctoral researcher at the Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington, advised by Prof. Hanna Hajishirzi. She is additionally supported by an Eric and Wendy Schmidt Postdoctoral Award. She obtained her PhD in Computer Science from the NLP lab at Bar Ilan University. Her work has been awarded an ACL Outstanding Paper Award and the ACL Best Theme Paper Award. During her doctoral studies, she conducted research internships at Google and the Allen Institute for AI, where she received the AI2 Outstanding Intern of the Year Award. She holds an MSc in AI from the University of Edinburgh and a BA from the University of Zurich. Valentina's research focuses on post-training and the adaptation of language models.

episodes.title: Open Science and LLMs, with Dr. Valentina Pyatkin

name: Sophia Simeng Han
title: PhD student at Yale University and Research Intern at Meta FAIR, USA
bio: Simeng Sophia Han is a final-year Ph.D. candidate at Yale University. She focuses on LLM complex reasoning, neuro-symbolic reasoning and reasoning evaluation. Her recent work on the FOLIO benchmark has had a profound impact on improving language models' reasoning capabilities. Outside of research, she deeply enjoys mentoring students, organizing conferences and workshops, and contributing to a more inclusive computer science community. She is also a chair for Widening NLP from 2025 to 2027. Beyond academia, Simeng is currently engaged in foundational research on LLM reasoning at Meta GenAI frontier reasoning team. She has also previously worked on information retrieval at Google DeepMind and retrieval-augmented generation at AWS NLP group.

episodes.title: Unlocking LLM Reasoning, with Simeng Sophia Han

name: Dr. Abhilasha Ravichander
title: Assistant Professor at the Max Planck Institute for Software Systems, Germany
bio: Until recently, Abhilasha Ravichander was a postdoctoral scholar at the University of Washington, and now she is a faculty member at the Max Planck Institute for Software Systems. She received her PhD from Carnegie Mellon University in 2022. Her research focuses on improving the robustness and transparency of large-scale language models. Abhilasha’s work has been presented at several top NLP conferences, receiving Best Resource Paper Award at ACL 2024, Best Theme Paper Award at ACL 2024, Best Paper Award at the Mid-Atlantic Student Colloquium 2024, Best Paper Award at the SoCalNLP 2022 symposium, Best Paper Award at the NAACL 2025 TrustNLP Workshop, and Area Chair Favorite Paper award at COLING 2018. She has been recognized as a 'Rising Star in Generative AI' (2024), 'Rising Star in EECS' (2022), and 'Rising Star in Data Science' (2021).

episodes.title: LLM Hallucinations and Machine Unlearning, with Dr. Abhilasha Ravichander

name: Dr. Dieuwke Hupkes
title: Research scientist at Meta AI Research, Netherlands
bio: Dr. Dieuwke Hupkes is a research scientist at Meta AI Research. She completed her PhD in computational linguistics at the Institute for Logic, Language and Computation (ILLC) at the University of Amsterdam under Willem Zuidema, followed by a postdoc at the Amsterdam unit of ELLIS. Her PhD at the University of Amsterdam focused on hierarchy and interpretability in neural models, exploring how AI systems can help us understand human language processing. And when she is not researching computational linguistics, she is competing in pole dancing championships, where she won the Dutch national title in doubles in 2018.

episodes.title: Generalization in AI, with Dr. Dieuwke Hupkes

name: Wanru Zhao
title: PhD student at the University of Cambridge, UK
bio: Wanru Zhao is a Ph.D. candidate in the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge, where she is supervised by Prof. Nic Lane in the Cambridge Machine Learning Systems Lab (CaMLSys). Her research focuses on democratizing large model development through distributed learning, data curation, and modular model design. She develops frameworks that enable organizations to jointly train and adapt models across data silos and heterogeneous compute, with the goal of making AI more accessible, efficient, and inclusive. Previously, she completed her M.Phil. in Advanced Computer Science at the University of Cambridge, graduating with Distinction.

episodes.title: Decentralized AI, with Wanru Zhao

name: Dr. Faiza Khan Khattak
title: CTO at Monark Health, Canada.
bio: Faiza is the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Monark Health, an innovative startup dedicated to leveraging AI to support individuals overcoming Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD), and she also works as an AI consultant. As a Natural Language Processing (NLP) scientist, Faiza specializes in fairness in language models, diverse NLP applications, and applied research, ensuring that AI technologies are equitable and inclusive. Faiza holds a Master’s and PhD in Computer Science from Columbia University. She further developed her expertise through postdoctoral research at the University Health Network (UHN) and St. Michael’s Hospital in Toronto and as a co-founder of a healthcare startup. She has also had the opportunity to teach as a sessional lecturer at the University of Toronto Scarborough. Her career spans both industry and academia, including roles as a Data Scientist at Manulife and an Applied Machine Learning Scientist at the Vector Institute for AI, where she has led cross-functional teams, directed collaborative research initiatives, and held workshops to bridge academic research with real-world applications. Her expertise extends to stakeholder engagement, AI adoption strategies, and mentoring junior team members. Faiza is also deeply committed to responsible AI development. She served as the lead organizer of the Responsible Language Models Workshop at the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) in 2024.

episodes.title: Interpretable AI, with Dr. Faiza Khan Khattak

name: Dr. Angelica Lim
title: Assistant Professor at Simon Fraser University, Canada.
bio: Dr. Angelica Lim is an AI roboticist. She is an Assistant Professor in Computing Science at Simon Fraser University and leads the SFU Rosie Lab, where she builds artificial intelligence software for robots to interact with social intelligence and empathy. Her research addresses the question 'Could a robot have feelings?' by combining neuroscience, machine learning and developmental psychology. Angelica has a Ph.D. and M.Sc. in Computer Science from Kyoto University, Japan, specializing in AI applied to Robotics, and a B.Sc. in Computing Science (specializing in Artificial Intelligence) from Simon Fraser University in Canada.

episodes.title: Robots with Empathy, with Dr. Angelica Lim

name: Aparna Balagopalan
title: PhD student at MIT, USA.
bio: Aparna Balagopalan is a PhD student in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) at MIT. Her research broadly focuses on developing fair, interpretable, and robust models by carefully re-evaluating and surfacing assumptions in machine learning-based measurements in socially-relevant contexts. Aparna has held research intern positions at the Stanford RegLab, the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy, the Technische Universität, Dresden as a DAAD-WISE scholar, and at the Philips Innovation Campus, Bengaluru in the healthcare R&D team.

episodes.title: Responsible AI for Health, with Aparna Balagopalan

name: Dr. Amanda Cercas Curry
title: Researcher at CENTAI Institute, Italy.
bio: Dr. Amanda Cercas Curry is a researcher at CENTAI Institute, where she is working on applied NLP, fairness and evaluation. Her research interests lie at the intersection of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) and Feminism with the aim of building more just NLP systems. She is particularly interested in ethics, with a strong influence from feminism. Previously she was a postdoctoral researcher at MilaNLP in Bocconi University. She completed her PhD at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh. She also co-hosts a podcast where she discusses all things tech ethics, called Let's Chat Ethics.

episodes.title: Bias in AI, with Dr. Amanda Cercas Curry

name: Dr. Nouha Dziri
title: Research scientist at Allen Institute for AI (AI2), USA.
bio: Dr. Nouha Dziri is an AI research scientist at the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2). Her research investigates a wide variety of problems across NLP and AI including building state-of-the-art language models and understanding their limits and inner workings. She also works on AI safety to ensure the responsible deployment of LLMs while enhancing their reasoning capabilities. Prior to Ai2, she worked at Google DeepMind and Microsoft Research. She earned her PhD from the University of Alberta and the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute. Her work has been published in top-tier AI venues including NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, TACL, ACL, NAACL and EMNLP, and featured in TechCrunch, LeMonde, The Economist, Science News and QuantaMagazine.

episodes.title: Limits of Transformers, with Dr. Nouha Dziri
